Has the ECU ever been reflashed, and are the headers, intake, exhaust and suspension factory original? Can you photograph the engine bay and the exhaust tips?
Is there any record of track or autocross use (track-day stickers, tow hook use, worn brake pads or rotors with heat cracks)?

Can you send a cold-start video from fully cold showing idle, plus a clip of a clean 3rd-gear pull?
Will the car be sold with a fresh California smog certificate dated within 90 days, and what is the documentation fee?
Are there any open Subaru recalls or campaigns on this VIN?
ppi_focus: Accident repair quality: paint-meter readings on every panel, panel gaps, overspray, replaced fasteners, frame rails, core support and the rear crash bar.
Underside on a lift: subframe and suspension-arm damage or bends, alignment readings, and any sign of lowering or curb strikes.
Clutch: engagement height, slip test in high gear, throwout bearing noise, and synchro feel (2nd and 3rd).
ECU scan: stored or pending codes, readiness monitors, and calibration ID versus stock to detect a current or removed tune.
Compression/leakdown and oil-consumption question, especially if there is any track evidence.
Brembo pads and rotors: thickness, heat checking, and brake fluid moisture content.
Tires: brand, matching set, date codes and wear pattern (inner-edge wear suggests alignment, lowering or crash damage).
Leaks: cam-plate and oil-pan seepage, differential and transmission seals.
SRS module status and airbag light behaviour given the accident report.
Cosmetic and interior wear consistent with 65.7k miles.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: a history report and repair invoice showing a minor, non-structural cosmetic event, plus a clean PPI with matched paint readings.
Up: service records, stock or verified-stock status, and tires with recent date codes.
Down: frame or structural involvement, airbag deployment, or poor repair quality found at PPI.
Down: evidence of a tune, track use, clutch slip, or a dealer refusal of an independent PPI.
Down: a branded title or an odometer inconsistency on the history report.
evidence.mission_note: A manual, naturally aspirated, top-spec BRZ inside the ideal budget band fits the enthusiast-bridge brief and should resell easily. The reported accident is the open question that governs both condition and resale.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes the car's identity: a VIN that decodes to a 2017 BRZ coupe 2.0L, consistent with the stated Limited/Performance Package spec, a 6-speed manual, Torsen LSD and 65,657 miles. The Autotrader history summary reports an accident or damage event and multiple owners. That is the only concrete condition datum, and its severity and repair quality are entirely open. The captured text gives no service records, tire data, or statement on modifications, track use or tune status. These are the model's main weak points and remain unverified, partly because the detail page was not captured. The 2013 valve-spring and 2018-2019 fuel-pump recalls are outside this car's model year per the profile, and the tracker found no open recalls. At $17,888 the asking price sits slightly above the $17,076 fair-value mid. That figure does not obviously reflect a discount for the reported accident.
evidence.next_action: Request the full Carfax/AutoCheck report and any accident repair invoice from California Motor Center, and confirm in writing that an independent PPI on a lift is allowed before any deposit.
